items.issue: Korean is grammatical and idiomatic (밥을 짓다 + 쌀로 collocation is correct), but the English gloss 'Mother cooks rice from grains' is awkward — 쌀 is itself uncooked rice, and rendering it as 'grains' obscures the 쌀(uncooked)/밥(cooked) distinction the sentence is illustrating. A learner reading the gloss won't know which Korean word was the target. Korean side: keep. English side: regloss.
items.suggestion: Regloss to 'Mother cooks rice (밥) from raw rice (쌀).' or 'Mother makes rice from uncooked rice grains.'

items.issue: 에브이 (Espeon) is the Korean rendering of Japanese エーフィー, derived from ESP/에스퍼 (psychic) + the Eevee evo-suffix. The Korean string 에브이 is not literally built from 이브이 (Eevee, 이브이 in Korean) — they share '브이' but begin with different syllables (에 vs 이), and the established etymology is ESP-based, not 'Eevee with a vowel swap'. Listing 이브이 'Eevee' as a component of 에브이 is at minimum imprecise (the shared piece is 브이, not 이브이) and arguably wrong (the productive root is 에스퍼/ESP).

suggestion.gloss: (component of Eevee-line names is 브이, not 이브이; or root is 에스퍼/ESP)
